seoTitle: How to Change a Microsoft Forms Name Easily (2026)
metaDescription: Rename a Microsoft Forms survey or quiz by editing the title inside the form editor. Covers why the dashboard's three-dot menu can't do it and what happens to your share link.
intro:
Microsoft Forms doesn't put a rename option on its dashboard. The tile grid under Recent, My forms, and Filled forms looks like it should have one, since most apps hide that kind of edit behind a right-click or a three-dot menu, but Forms doesn't work that way. The name lives inside the form itself, as the editable title at the top of the editor.

This guide shows where that title field actually sits, why the dashboard's own three-dot menu isn't it, and what does or doesn't change when you retitle a form partway through collecting responses.

steps.heading: Find the form on the dashboard
steps.body: Open forms.office.com and sign in. Your forms show up as tiles under tabs like Recent, My forms, and Filled forms, each labeled with its title, its owner group, and a running count of responses. Find the one you want to rename. You'll open it directly in the next step, not through its three-dot menu.

image.caption: The Forms dashboard under the Recent tab, listing saved forms as tiles with their response counts — including the form we're about to rename.

steps.heading: Skip the three-dot menu
steps.body: Hovering a tile reveals an ellipsis menu, and it's the natural place to look first. Microsoft's own support forum confirms what that menu actually contains: Open, Copy, Move to group, Favorite, and Remove from Recent. "Group" here means a Forms group workspace, not a folder, and there is no Rename entry among them. Clicking through that menu looking for one is the most common dead end in this task. Go straight to Open instead.

steps.heading: Open the form and click the title
steps.body: Click the tile to load the full editor. The form's name sits as a large header above the question list, and clicking directly on that text turns it into an active field with a blinking cursor. No edit button, no settings panel. The title is the input.

image.caption: A form's title sitting in the editor as an active editable field, with the cursor placed and ready to type.

steps.heading: Replace the text and let autosave catch it
steps.body: Select the existing title, delete it, and type the new one. There's no save button for this: press Enter, or click anywhere else on the canvas, and the editor's status indicator flashes "Saving…" before settling back to "Saved." If you're only fixing a typo, you don't need to clear the whole field. Click into the word and edit it in place.

image.caption: The title field cleared out mid-edit, ready for a new name to be typed in — the same click-to-edit behavior applies to every form.

steps.heading: Confirm the link still works, then preview
steps.body: A form's share link is built from its ID, not its title, so an existing link keeps working after a rename. Anyone who already has it will simply see the new name when they open it. Before telling people the form is ready, click Preview in the toolbar to check how the new title wraps on desktop and mobile. A replacement title that looks fine in the editor can crowd the header on a phone screen.

faq.question: Where's the rename option in Microsoft Forms?
faq.answer: There isn't a dedicated one. Open the form and click directly on its title text at the top of the editor; it becomes an editable field.

faq.question: Why doesn't the dashboard's three-dot menu have a rename option?
faq.answer: That menu is for Open, Copy, Move to group, Favorite, and Remove from Recent. It handles housekeeping across your form list, not editing an individual form.

faq.question: Will renaming a form break my share link or lose responses?
faq.answer: No. Both the link and the collected responses are tied to the form's underlying ID, which doesn't change when you edit the title.

faq.question: Do I need to save the new title manually?
faq.answer: No. Microsoft Forms saves it automatically as soon as you press Enter or click away from the title field, shown briefly by a "Saving…" indicator.

verifiedNote: Click path and screens come from a recorded walkthrough. In September 2026, the claim about the dashboard's three-dot menu was checked against Microsoft's own Q&A support forum, which lists that menu's actual contents as Open, Copy, Move to group, Favorite, and Remove from Recent, with no Rename entry. Microsoft's official support pages on creating and naming forms were also checked; Microsoft has not published a dedicated article for renaming an existing form, so this guide relies on the click-to-edit title behavior shown in the recording plus that forum confirmation.
